column3: “Abram was very wealthy” states his condition without an explicit verb of becoming.
The herdsmen are named in the order “my herdsmen and your herdsmen,” following “between me and you.”
“Lot lifted his eyes” preserves the upward-looking image rendered “looked out.”
The direction is rendered “from the east” in the literal reading, instead of “toward the east”; the separation is “each from his brother,” rather than explicitly naming Abram and Lot.
“Your seed” preserves the collective image rendered “your offspring.”
